title: Journey - Seven Nights of Rest - Night 4: He gives sleep

parts.style: warm, soft bedtime welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Seven Nights of Rest. <short pause> This is night four, He Gives Sleep. <short pause> The day is Yours. I am counted. I am covered. <short pause> Tonight we stop at the desk, where one small lamp is still on... because somebody is still trying.

Sometimes we even work at sleeping. <short pause> We watch the clock. We do the sums. <short pause> If I drop off now, I'll get five hours. <short pause> And the harder we try, the further away it goes. <short pause> The same psalm that sent the watchman home has a word for tired workers, in Psalm one hundred twenty-seven, verse two.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.

parts.style: tender, soft, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: Notice who does the giving. <short pause> Sleep is His gift, so it can't be earned. <short pause> And if it comes slowly, you are no less His beloved. <short pause> Lying awake is not a failing. <short pause> If it happens night after night, you can ask a doctor for help... and be beloved there, too.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Jesus once told of a farmer who scattered seed, and went to bed. <short pause> He was speaking of God's kingdom, but we can borrow the picture. <short pause> The farmer sleeps, and the seed grows, he doesn't know how. <short pause> Choose one thing you planted today. <short pause> Leave it in the dark soil with God... and take your hands away.

parts.style: prayerful, very slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Giver of sleep, I stop trying. <short pause> Grow what I cannot grow. <short pause> I will take rest as it comes, a little or a lot, from Your hand. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, very slow goodnight, resting between phrases
parts.text: Turn the clock to the wall, and put out the lamp on the desk. <short pause> The day is Yours... <short pause> I am counted... <short pause> I am covered... <short pause> Sleep is a gift. <short pause> Goodnight, beloved.
